timeline.title: Week 1: Foundational Aptitude & Basic Programming Logic
timeline.description: Establish a strong base in Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning, and familiarize with Programming Logic/Pseudo Code. Focus on understanding core concepts.
tasks: **Quantitative Aptitude (1.5 hours/day):** Number Systems, HCF & LCM, Percentages, Profit & Loss. Solve ~20-30 basic problems daily.
**Reasoning Ability (1 hour/day):** Series (Number/Alphabet), Coding-Decoding, Analogies, Direction Sense. Solve ~15-20 questions daily.

**Programming Logic / Pseudo Code (0.5 hours/day):** Understand basic programming constructs (variables, data types, if-else, loops). Practice writing simple pseudo-code for given problems. Watch introductory videos on C/C++/Python basic syntax (choose one language for NQT coding).
Set up a dedicated study space and environment.
Familiarize with the TCS NQT exam pattern and syllabus.
Create a daily study schedule to adhere to for the next 4 weeks.

timeline.title: Week 2: Advanced Aptitude, Reasoning & Basic Coding
timeline.description: Deep dive into more complex aptitude and reasoning topics. Start actual coding practice with fundamental data structures and algorithms relevant to NQT.
tasks: **Quantitative Aptitude (1 hour/day):** Time & Work, Time, Speed & Distance, Averages, Mixtures & Allegations. Solve 15-20 problems daily.
**Reasoning Ability (1 hour/day):** Syllogisms, Blood Relations, Seating Arrangements (linear). Solve 15-20 questions daily.

**Programming Logic / Coding (1 hour/day):** Practice basic coding problems in your chosen language (C/C++/Python) focusing on arrays, strings, conditional statements, and loops. Understand basic data structures like arrays and their operations. Practice debugging simple code snippets.
Dedicate 30 mins daily to Verbal Ability: Grammar rules (Subject-Verb Agreement, Tenses), Vocabulary building (5-10 words/day), Reading Comprehension (1 passage daily).
Attempt a sectional mock test (Aptitude OR Reasoning OR Coding) to gauge progress and identify weak areas.

timeline.title: Week 3: Problem Solving, NQT Specifics & Speed Building
timeline.description: Focus on NQT-specific question types, advanced problem-solving techniques, and improving speed and accuracy. Integrate verbal ability more rigorously.
tasks: **Quantitative Aptitude (1 hour/day):** Permutations & Combinations, Probability, Data Interpretation (Tables, Graphs). Solve 15-20 problems daily with a timer.
**Reasoning Ability (1 hour/day):** Complex Puzzles (Circular/Box arrangements), Critical Reasoning, Data Sufficiency. Solve 15-20 problems daily.

**Programming Logic / Coding (1 hour/day):** Practice NQT-style coding questions (e.g., problems involving common algorithms like sorting, searching, basic recursion). Focus on writing efficient code and understanding time/space complexity intuitively. Practice output prediction questions.
**Verbal Ability (30 mins/day):** Error Identification, Sentence Correction, Para Jumbles, advanced Reading Comprehension passages. Focus on speed and accuracy.
Attempt 2-3 previous year TCS NQT coding questions.

timeline.title: Week 4: Revision, Mock Tests & Strategy
timeline.description: Intensive revision of all topics, taking full-length mock tests, analyzing performance, and refining exam strategy.
tasks: **Full Revision (1 hour/day):** Revisit all formulas, concepts, and common problem-solving techniques for Aptitude, Reasoning, and Verbal. Review notes and previous mistakes.

**Mock Tests & Analysis (2 hours/day):** Take at least 3-4 full-length TCS NQT mock tests (each approx. 2-3 hours). Dedicate significant time (1 hour per mock) to analyzing your performance, understanding incorrect answers, and identifying persistent weak areas.
Focus on improving speed for sections where you are slow and accuracy for sections where you make careless mistakes.
Practice time management strategies for the actual exam.
Refine your strategy for attempting different sections (e.g., which section to attempt first, how much time to allocate to each question type).
Stay calm and confident; avoid learning new major topics in the last few days.

skillsToLearn: Quantitative Aptitude (Number Systems, Algebra, Geometry, P&C, Probability, DI)
Reasoning Ability (Logical, Verbal, Data Interpretation, Puzzles)
Verbal Ability (Grammar, Vocabulary, Reading Comprehension, Sentence Correction)
Programming Logic (Pseudo Code, Flowcharts, Output Prediction)
Coding (Basic Data Structures - Arrays, Strings; Fundamental Algorithms - Searching, Sorting, Recursion, Problem-solving)

resources.name: TCS NQT Official Website (for syllabus & exam pattern)
Quantitative Aptitude for Competitive Examinations by R.S. Aggarwal
A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning by R.S. Aggarwal

habits: Follow a consistent daily study schedule for 3 hours.
Solve problems daily from all sections (Aptitude, Reasoning, Coding).
Analyze mistakes thoroughly and maintain an 'error log' or 'mistake notebook'.
Take short breaks (5-10 mins) after every 50-60 mins of study to avoid burnout.
Regularly revise concepts, especially formulas and shortcuts.
Stay hydrated and ensure adequate sleep.

daily: Complete 1.5 hours of Aptitude & Reasoning practice.
Complete 0.5-1 hour of Programming Logic / Coding practice.
Dedicate 30 mins to Verbal Ability (grammar, vocab, RC).
Solve at least 5-10 problems from weak areas identified.
weekly: Attempt at least one sectional or full-length mock test.
Analyze mock test performance and identify weak topics/areas.
Revise all concepts learned during the week.
Practice previous year's NQT questions for relevant sections.
Track progress and adjust study plan if needed.
